paras: The attempted lynching of Fritz W. Haas and Catherine Hoffart was a threat by a crowd at Union, Franklin County, Missouri, in late February or early March 1881 against two prisoners held in the county jail on a murder indictment. Officers removed the pair by night to St. Louis, and no one was hurt. The episode is known only from a single wire paragraph carried by several papers in Tennessee, Mississippi, Arkansas, Missouri and Indiana.

Haas and Hoffart, whom the wire item called "his alleged paramour," were confined in the Franklin County Jail at Union under indictment for the murder of Mrs. Haas. The brief gives no details of the killing, of when the indictment was returned, or of the race of either prisoner.

According to the dispatch, the two "narrowly escaped lynching at the hands of an infuriated crowd." The item does not describe an assault on the jail, give the size of the crowd, or name anyone in it. Under cover of darkness, officers got the prisoners out of town and took them to St. Louis, where, the dispatch said, they were "now safe at least from mob violence."
No report of arrests among the crowd, of the prisoners' return to Union, or of a murder trial appears in the coverage.

The story reached readers as one unheadlined paragraph in national news-summary columns. The Southern Standard of McMinnville, Tennessee, and the American Citizen of Canton, Mississippi, both printed it on March 5, 1881, under "Late News Items," between reports of a British defeat by the Boers and an orphan asylum fire. The Batesville Guard in Arkansas ran it on March 9, the Iron County Register of Ironton, Missouri, on March 10 under "Personal and General," and the Jasper Weekly Courier in Indiana on March 11 under "Crimes and Casualties."

Every copy used the same wording, treating the murder charge as an indictment rather than a proven fact and offering no comment on the crowd. Even the one Missouri paper found, the Ironton weekly, printed the wire text with only a one-word change, adding no local detail. No Black-press coverage of the episode is available.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Fritz W. Haas and Catherine Hoffart
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: An 'infuriated crowd' sought to lynch two jailed murder defendants, who 'narrowly escaped lynching' when officers removed them to St. Louis (A1).
No one was killed: the crowd threatened two prisoners indicted for murder, but officers removed them to St. Louis (A1); it is a threatened or attempted lynching, not a completed one.
All five copies (A1-A5) are the same wire brief, word for word; no independent local, St. Louis or follow-up account was found.
